Today's international headlines:
- US envoys set for Ukraine talks after meeting Putin in Russia: Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner left Moscow having "discussed substantive plans for next steps" with Putin, according to the White House.
- US and Iran trade retaliatory attacks on ships as conflict flares: The US says it hit three Iranian oil tankers, while Iran says it targeted three US-linked ships.
- TV presenter among 11 sentenced to death in Egypt drugs case: Sarah Khalifa is best known for her TV programme Mission Impossible which dealt with crime issues.
- Volcano eruption triggers flight suspensions at Indonesia's main airport: More than 20,000 passengers are stranded after ash was detected in airspace near Jakarta following volcanic eruptions.
- Watch: Moment 64-year-old Nepali woman is found alive in mud-buried home: Chandika Shrestha was airlifted to hospital after spending more than 10 days in her partially buried house.
- Prince William to attend King Harald's funeral in Norway: The Prince of Wales will represent the King at the funeral of Harald V in Oslo next week.
- Trump signs order to remove endangered species protection for grey wolves: The US president says the move will help ranchers, but conservationists say it could derail efforts to recover populations.
- Nepal rescuers try to reach dozens trapped in tunnel after two found alive: More than 1,300 people have died and thousands are missing, but rescuers' hopes have risen after finding survivors in a tunnel.
- 'He was a lifeline' - Families at a loss after Haitian caregivers let go in US: Haitian immigrants make up a large portion of the already overburdened home-care workforce.
- Majority Russian-speaking city in Ukraine considers language ban in the arts: Ukraine's third-biggest city Odesa decides this week whether to ban Russian-language content in music and literature in public.
- Aviation faces hotter, stormier skies – and passengers might have to accept more disruption: Are people going to have to increasingly accept more delays and diversions as the effects of climate change intensify?
- What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong: As the UN adopts a new world map to reflect Africa's true size, let's take a closer look at what different maps get right and wrong.
